scope.unmappedReferenceIssueReason: The snapshot includes test projects that are not declared by the Zenith client configuration; retain them in the frozen audit fixture, but do not place them under a Zenith board root.

knowledgeRowRepresentation.rowId: A stable source row id in row frontmatter; this is the value accepted by resolve commands.

knowledgeRowRepresentation.values: A property-name map in row frontmatter. SELECT and MULTI_SELECT cells store option ids; readers resolve ids to labels using vault.config.json knowledge property options.
knowledgeRowRepresentation.body: Optional Markdown prose is retained in the row entry only when the source has no structured property for it.

ticket.rawIssueRow: ticket frontmatter.source contains every jira.issues column; for non-null description the exporter removes source.description and writes it as UTF-8 Markdown body, while a null description remains source.description=null.

relationRows.jira.comments: metadata.md.tables.jira.comments; current exporter does not synthesize a body comment sentinel

sprint.rawRow: frontmatter.source is the complete jira.sprints row; goal and date fields are read from source until an ergonomic writer emits them directly.

catalogs.versions: <boardRoot>/versions.md frontmatter.rows[]; rows are complete jira.versions records

history.rows: frontmatter.rows[] is the complete jira.issue_activity subset for issues exported under that board root

supporting.tables: All captured source tables except the per-board exported jira issue/sprint/catalog/workflow/history rows are retained under frontmatter.tables; rows belonging to non-mapped project/workflow scopes are retained under frontmatter.archivedTables.
supporting.knowledge: notion.projects, notion.databases, notion.database_properties and notion.database_rows remain source rows here in the current fixture; notion.pages is not extracted because local Markdown documents replace the Notion page mirror. No board-specific knowledge/*.md files are emitted yet.
supporting.documents: Local Markdown files are scanned directly as document records; they are not reconstructed from notion.pages rows.
supporting.identities: public.users, public.organizations and public.memberships remain source rows here; vault.config.json carries local policy and board roots.
supporting.config: agent.config.json and zagent.project.json policy is embedded under vault.config.json:policy. The current export does not synthesize the future identities/knowledge config sections; readers use metadata rows when present.
supporting.ordering: metadata.md frontmatter.ordering.links and frontmatter.ordering.history map each source jira issue id to observed legacy link/activity row ids in capture order. These ids preserve display ordering only; they are not canonical relation or history state.

fixtureScope.isolatedProjects: Reference-only projects (including AT433D and ATC047) remain in the audit fixture and are never treated as mapped Zenith boards.

normalization.note: The rules below describe the implemented Stage 1 read-only exporter and readers. They deliberately do not turn future writer policies into current validation or silently normalize values that the legacy payloads compare exactly.

rules.rule: The exporter persists key as <project.key>-<issue.number>; the source issue id remains provenance in ticket frontmatter.source.id and metadata tables. CLI lookup may use its case-insensitive fallback, but it does not rewrite the persisted key.
rules.effect: Project and issue surrogate ids are not vault addresses; the canonical key is the address used by read commands.
rules.futureProposal: Duplicate keys already cause repo-wide index diagnostics and claim refusal; future writers must preserve that invariant.

rules.rule: The exporter projects known foreign keys to project keys, ticket keys, names, or user emails in canonical frontmatter and retains source ids in source/metadata. Readers resolve current joins through the index and preserve null or raw source values when a projection is absent.
rules.effect: The scanner rejects unresolved parent, sprint, block target, canonical link target, status, and fixVersion references, and checks assignees against retained identities. These diagnostics make the repository unclaimable.
rules.futureProposal: Future writers must reuse the scanner reference checks before persisting edits.

rules.rule: The current exporter writes sprint slug as lowercase project key plus '-' plus the source sprint id: <project.key.toLowerCase()>-<sprint.id>. It does not derive the slug from sprint.name or apply Unicode NFKC/name slugging; name remains the display field and ticket sprint stores this id-based slug.
rules.effect: The id-based slug is the actual Stage 1 sprint file and reference identity.
rules.futureProposal: A name-derived Unicode slug and a collision policy may be designed for a future writer; neither is implemented in the snapshot.

rules.rule: The current exporter writes complete jira.versions rows to <boardRoot>/versions.md. Ticket fixVersions is the captured array of FIX version names; version list readers derive membership from current canonical names scoped to the project, while jira.issue_versions remains audit provenance.
rules.effect: No version slug is generated or required in the actual snapshot; version ids are catalog provenance and names are the canonical ticket references.
rules.futureProposal: A stable version slug could be added by a future writer after its identity and collision rules are reviewed.

rules.rule: The exporter writes ticket labels from snapshot.labelOrder[issue.id] when supplied, otherwise from jira.issue_labels traversal joined to jira.labels.name. The captured array order is preserved; labels are not sorted by normalization.
rules.effect: Readers preserve label order and retain label ids and catalog rows in metadata; no label is reordered or guessed.
rules.futureProposal: A future writer may choose a canonical sort order, but that would be a format change rather than current read behavior.

rules.rule: The exporter writes BLOCKS relations to frontmatter.blocks and other types to frontmatter.links with target key, type where applicable, and reason. The links reader always enumerates canonical outgoing links and derives incoming links from every canonical source ticket; metadata.ordering.links[issueSourceId] contains observed legacy link ids/order, and an edge absent from that capture has id null.
rules.effect: Canonical frontmatter edits to target, type, reason, additions, or removals are visible to reads; source relation rows supply stable ids/order for captured edges only. This rule does not assert duplicate-triple, dangling-target, or nonblank-reason validation.
rules.futureProposal: A future writer or scanner may add explicit relation validation once its diagnostic contract is defined.

rules.rule: Exported source timestamp text is retained. Sprint and version payloads restore the legacy SQL text form by replacing the leading date/time 'T' with a space while preserving captured fractional precision; history compares parseable values at UTC microsecond precision (a missing offset defaults to UTC) and emits ISO UTC strings at millisecond precision. Null remains null.
rules.effect: Timestamp formatting is command-specific and exact: readers do not rewrite every surface to one RFC 3339 form or apply a broad equivalent-instant normalization.
rules.futureProposal: A future writer may choose one timestamp representation only after preserving the legacy payload contract explicitly.

rules.rule: A description beginning with the captured \x bytea form is hex-decoded; other descriptions are UTF-8 encoded, and a lossy UTF-8 decode causes export failure. The decoded text is written as the Markdown body without a general line-ending normalization.
rules.effect: Source.description stays in source when null; non-null description moves to the body in the captured decoded text. No editor-model no-op-save guarantee is implemented.
rules.futureProposal: A future writer may specify line-ending and byte-preservation behavior separately.

rules.rule: The read-only fixture retains captured notion.database_properties option records. For a SELECT property, a row reader resolves an exact option id to its captured label; an id with no matching option remains visible as the raw id. No option id is generated during export.
rules.effect: The reader does not guess labels and does not claim a doctor error for an orphaned option id; current handling is preservation for inspection.
rules.futureProposal: The optionId(label) algorithm and validation for missing ids, including MULTI_SELECT behavior, require a future writer/doctor contract.

rules.rule: Captured source/catalog order is retained in exported arrays. metadata.ordering.links[issueSourceId] and metadata.ordering.history[issueSourceId] retain observed legacy ids/order from the frozen capture. Readers use those observations only where required for legacy output: links sort captured ids and append new edges; history uses observed ids for equal-timestamp ties; sprint/version catalogs sort source position then name; rows/suggestions sort newest created_at and preserve stored order for ties; queue uses its command-specific priority/position/key order.
rules.effect: There is no broad array sorting or extra tie-break normalization. The observed ordering maps carry ids/order only and never override current canonical field edits.
rules.futureProposal: Any additional deterministic ordering must be added to the command matrix and captured metadata explicitly.

rules.rule: SQL NULL is retained in source rows. Canonical fields that the exporter explicitly projects with a null fallback are YAML null; optional values that are undefined may be omitted by YAML serialization. Empty text, false, and zero are not converted to null.
rules.effect: Unset, empty, false, zero, and null remain distinguishable wherever the source and payload contract expose them.
rules.futureProposal: A future writer may define omission rules per field, but it must not silently collapse these values.

crossEntityRules.rule: Any parse failure, duplicate key, dangling blocks target, dangling sprint, dangling parent, or unresolved reference in any board root refuses all claims until fixed.
A BLOCKS edge is stored only in the source ticket; incoming blockedBy is derived by index.
workflow.md preserves statuses and transitions; rules, screens, columns, and quick filters are not read by retained commands.
Knowledge row SELECT cells use option ids internally and are resolved to labels for rows output and where matching.
issue_activity is frozen under history/pre-migration.md; post-cutover history is git log.
No HTTP contract, bearer token, docsTree upload, Yjs socket, or Notion URL is part of the vault CLI interface.
Entities marked dropped-empty must be checked empty by export; a nonempty source row is an export error requiring a reviewed mapping.
The 56 schema tables exported by database/schema/index.ts are listed above; figma and mermaid are explicitly out-of-scope-untouched rather than silently omitted.
